elements.element: Customer is not obligated to procure hosted analytics services exclusively from Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 expressly appoints Vendor as “a non-exclusive provider” and permits Customer to procure equivalent services from any third party. Section 12.3 also states that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment.

elements.element: Vendor is not designated as Customer’s sole supplier or provider.
elements.evidence: The sole-provider designation has been removed from Section 2.2 and replaced with a non-exclusive appointment.

elements.element: If any exclusivity obligation binds Customer, it is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation binds Customer: Section 2.2 is expressly non-exclusive, and Section 12.3 confirms that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment. The condition requiring a category limitation is therefore demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If any exclusivity obligation binds Customer, it lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation binds Customer, so there is no exclusivity duration requiring a 12-month limit.

elements.element: If any exclusivity obligation binds Customer, it ends automatically upon Vendor’s failure to meet applicable service levels.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation binds Customer, so the condition requiring an automatic service-level-failure termination mechanism is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If any exclusivity obligation binds Customer, it ends automatically upon Vendor’s failure to meet applicable delivery dates.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation binds Customer, so the condition requiring an automatic delivery-failure termination mechanism is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The operative redline fully achieves the preferred position by replacing the sole and exclusive appointment with an expressly non-exclusive appointment and an affirmative third-party procurement right. Because no exclusivity remains, the conditional fallback limitations are unnecessary and are satisfied by the demonstrable absence of their triggering condition. The change is narrowly directed to exclusivity, preserves Vendor’s appointment as a provider, and resolves the original conflict with Section 12.3.
